title: Reconstruction Contract Cancellation Clause and the Buyer's Cooling-Off Right
content:
**Clause 1 — status.** A Reconstruction contract must be in signed status when it is cancelled. Cancelling is the customer's own act.

**Clause 2 — free cancellation.** A cancellation is free of charge only when the contract was signed at the customer's home for at least the cooling-off minimum amount and the customer cancels no later than the cooling-off period after the customer signed the contract. The cooling-off period is counted in business days, which for this right are every calendar day except Sundays and federal holidays, starting the day after the signed date, and a cancellation made on the last such day is in time. This is the buyer's right under the Federal Trade Commission's Cooling-Off Rule for sales made at the buyer's home; within it every draw already paid is refunded and nothing is charged.

**Clause 3 — cancellation fee.** Any other cancellation of a signed contract before the permit stage carries the cancellation fee, the tier's cancellation fee percentage of the contract amount, plus the restocking percentage of the cost of any special-order materials already ordered. The cancellation fee is booked as the tier's cancellation fee percentage of the contract amount, rounded to the cent.

**Clause 4 — after the permit stage.** A contract already permitted or in construction cannot be cancelled by the desk; such a request is handed to a human representative as not covered by policy.

## The free-cancellation test

All three must hold, each read from the contract record (the signed date, the place of signing and the contract amount), not from the customer's account:

| Signed at the customer's home | Contract amount at or above the cooling-off minimum | Cancelled no later than the last cooling-off business day | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Yes | Free: every draw already paid is refunded, nothing is charged |
| No | any | any | Cancellation fee and restocking |
| Yes | No | any | Cancellation fee and restocking |
| Yes | Yes | No | Cancellation fee and restocking |

## Counting the period

- The clock starts from the signed date on the contract; that day itself is not counted.
- Counting begins on the day after the signed date; each calendar day that is not a Sunday and not a federal holiday counts as one business day.
- The period ends on the last counted business day; a cancellation on that day is in time, and a cancellation on any later day is not.

**Boundary cases (hypothetical, assuming no federal holiday falls in the period and a three-business-day period).** A contract signed at the customer's home on a Thursday: Friday is business day one, Saturday is business day two, Sunday is not counted, Monday is business day three. A cancellation on that Monday is in time; a cancellation on the Tuesday is late.

## Fee example (hypothetical figures)

A contract of $21,000.00 signed at the company office and cancelled while still in signed status, with special-order cabinets already ordered at an assumed cost of $2,400.00, an assumed fee percentage of 10% and an assumed restocking percentage of 25%: the cancellation fee is $2,100.00 and the restocking charge is $600.00.
